Each frame steps the top rider then the bottom one; while the times differ, marks the rider with the smaller time as the leader; ends when both have finished and both speeds are zero.
After the race: draws both meters, waits 255 frames or for fire, silences the SID and waits for fire to be let go.

Every second frame reads the rider's stick, or the pacer's choice, turns it into a quarter of the crank's turn, and speeds the rider up by 1, to 16, when it is the quarter the crank is in; the speed falls by 1 each time its countdown runs out.
Reads the rider's joystick: stick_swap picks the port, so the first button pressed at the start decides who steers which rider.

A player whose speed has fallen below 2 is put back at 2 once their time has reached five seconds; with the slow-down that follows, the speed swings between 1 and 2 and never reaches 0 before the finish.

The music driver, called each frame: for a new tune reads which voices it uses and starts each at its notes. Then for each voice, when its note's time is up, reads the voice's next bytes: $FF ends it, $FE lo hi jumps, $FD n sets the length of the notes, a byte below $80 is a note (an index into the frequency table, $7F a rest) followed by how many times the set length it lasts, and $FC is followed by pairs of a SID register and its value, until a byte of $80 or more.
